calls.head: Strength against strength
calls.body: The Senators are near the top of the league for chance quality, and the Maple Leafs are near the top of the league at preventing dangerous shots. Our lean: the Senators’ chance quality wins out.
calls.call: The Senators’ chances are more dangerous than the league average (a 6.3% chance of scoring on the average shot) against the Maple Leafs.
calls.nums: Ottawa 6th for chance quality (a 6.6% chance of scoring on the average shot) · Toronto 7th for preventing dangerous shots
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 0 and 2 games this season
calls.happened: On chance quality, Ottawa had 11.4% a shot. The league average is 6.3% a shot, and they came in at 6.6% a shot.

calls.head: Bobrovsky’s record against the Senators is a coincidence
calls.body: Since 2023-24, Bobrovsky has been a wall against the Senators, well above his usual. Fans love a pattern like this, but we checked three seasons of them and they predicted nothing. Expect the usual Bobrovsky.
calls.call: If Bobrovsky starts, his save percentage lands closer to his usual .900 than to his .935 against the Senators.
calls.nums: 9 starts against Ottawa: .935 save percentage · .900 against everyone else
calls.cite: Goalie starts since 2023-24 · 9 against Ottawa, 3,966 shots against everyone else
calls.happened: S. Bobrovsky stopped 26 of 29 shots (.897), against his usual .900 and his .935 against this team before tonight.

calls.head: The Senators lock it down; the Maple Leafs don’t
calls.body: The Senators are one of the league’s best for shot suppression, at the stingy end; the Maple Leafs are the league’s worst, at the porous end. Expect that gap to show.
calls.call: The Senators allow fewer 5-on-5 shot attempts per 60 than the Maple Leafs.
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 0 and 2 games this season
calls.happened: On 5-on-5 shot attempts allowed per 60, Ottawa had 69.1 per 60 and Toronto 45.6 per 60. Coming in, Ottawa was at 51.7 per 60 and Toronto at 62.9 per 60.

TOR.head: We gave Toronto only a 29% chance, and it went the way we feared.

OTT.head: We gave Ottawa a 71% chance, and Ottawa delivered.

surprises.head: Ottawa got the good looks
surprises.body: Ottawa’s shots at 5-on-5 were more dangerous than usual: an 11.4% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 6.6% (league average 6.3%). A team strays this far about once every 600 games.

surprises.head: Toronto flipped the shot count
surprises.body: Toronto took 60% of the 5-on-5 shot attempts (adjusted for score and venue). From how these two usually play, Toronto would expect about 42%. A team strays this far about once every 175 games.
surprises.flipped: The Senators lock it down; the Maple Leafs don’t

story.head: The Senators beat the Maple Leafs
paras: Thomas Chabot opened the scoring late in the first. The game was tied twice. Stephen Halliday scored the winner midway through the third.
The score was fair. Replay this game’s chances a hundred times and the Senators win about seven in ten.

items.text: Two of the preview’s three calls held.
